guideTitle: 6 Best Ultrasonic Cleaners for Dentures in 2026
metaDescription: We compared six compact ultrasonic cleaners for dentures and dental appliances on frequency, modes, noise, tank size and included accessories for daily use.
introParagraphs: Dentures collect food film and stain in small ridges that a brush can miss, and holding a slippery appliance under a tap while scrubbing is a chore many wearers would happily skip. A countertop ultrasonic pod soaks the denture in water and uses tiny bubbles to loosen residue, so your hands do less of the work. These pods look similar online, but frequency, cycle options, noise and tank fit differ in ways that matter for a larger appliance.

We evaluated six pods based on product specs and buyer feedback, comparing frequency, cycle options, UV features, stated noise level, tank size and included accessories. Frequencies run from 42,000 Hz to 48kHz and nearly every pod has a 200 ml tank, so check that your denture will sit in the liquid without pressing on the walls. This is a convenience comparison and not medical advice, so follow your dentist's care instructions for your own appliance.
Use the picks to narrow the field, then work through the buying criteria and tables. Never use hot water or harsh chemicals unless your denture maker says they are safe.

products.name: 7MAGIC 48kHz Ultrasonic Denture and Retainer Cleaner

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Quick 5, Deep 10, Clean Only 10, UV Only 10 min

products.description:
The 7MAGIC is the most complete pod in this group. It runs at 48 kHz and offers four clear modes, Quick Clean at 5 minutes, Deep Clean at 10 minutes, Clean Only at 10 minutes and UV Only at 10 minutes, with a countdown display and a breathing light. Four UV-C lights switch off automatically when the lid opens, and the 200 ml SUS 304 tank is rated IPX5 for bathroom splashes.

The kit is generous, with a basket, tweezers, a brush, a cloth, a power adapter and six cleaning tablets in the box. The listing says water is enough for routine care and a tablet helps with heavier buildup. The tradeoff is the same as every pod here, a 200 ml tank is snug for a full denture, so measure before you buy.

Daily use is a fill, press and rinse routine, and the lid-open shutoff on the UV lights is a thoughtful safety touch. At below 42 dB it is quieter than the 45 dB-class UEOFEN and ACMEZING. Against the Zima it offers more modes and a fixed 48 kHz setting.
products.bestFor: Denture and retainer wearers who want a well-equipped, quiet pod with a clear four-mode layout.
pros: Four clear modes include a 10-minute clean-only run without UV
Listed at below 42 dB, quiet enough for a bathroom or bedside table
IPX5 water resistance copes with everyday sink and counter splashes
A basket, tweezers, brush, cloth and six tablets come in the box
cons: The 200 ml tank is tight for a full denture and may touch the walls
UV-C lights are an extra and do not replace rinsing the appliance
A fixed 48 kHz setting does not adapt like the Zima's frequency

products.name: ACMEZING DeepClean 45kHz Retainer Cleaner with UV-C

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: 5 and 10 minute clean, 5 and 10 minute pulse

products.description:
The ACMEZING DeepClean pairs 45 kHz ultrasonic cleaning with four UV-C lights placed to give more even coverage in the chamber. It offers four modes, a 5-minute quick clean, a 10-minute deep clean, and 5-minute or 10-minute pulse options, and the 200 ml tank is said to hold up to three retainers at once.

The pulse modes are gentler, which suits thin trays, while the noise is rated at about 45 dB. The listing mentions silicone shock-absorbing pads and a reinforced stainless steel build. The honest limit is that holding three small retainers is not the same as holding a full denture, so it is best for a household with several small appliances.

Setup is simple, and the compact footprint suits a bathroom counter, a desk or a dorm room. Compared with the 7MAGIC at below 42 dB it is a little louder, and next to the UEOFEN at 45 kHz it adds pulse modes. It makes a smart pick for a family or for someone who rotates between a retainer, a guard and a partial.
products.bestFor: Households with several small appliances that want pulse modes and UV-C in one pod.
pros: The 200 ml tank is said to hold up to three retainers at once
Pulse modes of 5 and 10 minutes offer a gentler cycle on thin trays
Four UV-C lights are positioned for more even coverage in the chamber
Silicone shock-absorbing pads help limit vibration on a bathroom counter
cons: Noise is about 45 dB, which is louder than the below-42 dB 7MAGIC
Holding three small retainers is not the same as fitting a full denture
UV-C is a convenience feature and does not replace rinsing by hand

products.name: UEOFEN 45kHz Dental Cleaning Pod, 200 ml with UV

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: 5 min quick, 10 min enhanced (5 pulse, 5 continuous)

products.description:
The UEOFEN keeps things simple with two modes. A 5-minute quick clean handles the daily refresh, and a 10-minute enhanced clean runs 5 minutes of pulse followed by 5 minutes of continuous ultrasonic. The 45 kHz output is paired with built-in 254nm UV lights, and a digital countdown timer shows progress.

The 200 ml water chamber has two side slots that hold items with handles, such as toothbrush heads, and a tweezer is included for lifting out a wet appliance. The listing says the UV can be used alone or with cleaning tablets for heavier buildup. With only two cycles it gives less variety than the four-mode 7MAGIC or ACMEZING, but fewer choices means less to learn.

It runs below 45 dB, so it is audible in a silent room but not intrusive. Compared with the ACMEZING at four modes and the same 45 kHz, it trades flexibility for ease. A full denture may not fit comfortably in 200 ml, so it suits partials, retainers and guards better.
products.bestFor: Wearers who want a short daily cycle and an enhanced option without extra settings.
pros: Two clear modes of 5 and 10 minutes keep every cycle easy to choose
The enhanced mode blends 5 minutes of pulse with 5 of continuous output
A digital countdown timer shows progress through every cleaning cycle
Side slots hold toothbrush heads, and a tweezer is included for lifting
cons: Only two modes, so there is less variety than the four-mode pods
Its below-45 dB rating is audible in a very quiet room at night
The 200 ml chamber may be a tight squeeze for a full-size denture

products.name: CXRUY 45kHz Ultrasonic Retainer Cleaner, Gloss Black

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: 5 min ultrasonic plus UV, 10 min pulsed plus UV

products.description:
The CXRUY is a 45 kHz pod with four UV lamps and two working modes, a 5-minute ultrasonic plus UV cycle and a 10-minute pulsed ultrasonic plus UV cycle. A green indicator marks when the UV is on. Its 200 ml tank is described as suitable for retainers, mouthguards, aligners, dentures and electric toothbrush heads.

The standout is overheat protection, which shuts the unit off automatically if the internal temperature reaches 100°C. The listing claims noise is reduced by 60%, which is a marketing figure with no baseline, so we did not rely on it. Like the UEOFEN it offers only two cycles, and there is no stated water-resistance rating.

It is a straightforward counter pod, and the gloss black finish is a matter of taste. Against the 7MAGIC with IPX5 and four modes, it gives you less flexibility but still covers the same daily use. Compared with the MUAYSY it keeps the same 45 kHz but simplifies the cycle choice, which suits anyone who wants set-and-forget operation.
products.bestFor: Daily wearers who want a simple two-mode pod with built-in overheat shutoff.
pros: Automatic shutoff triggers if the internal temperature reaches 100°C
Two modes include a 10-minute pulsed ultrasonic cycle paired with UV
The 200 ml tank is described as suited to dentures, guards and trays
A green indicator makes the UV status easy to see at a glance
cons: Only two cycles, so there is less choice than the 7MAGIC or MUAYSY
The noise reduction figure has no baseline, so treat it as marketing

products.name: Zima Dental Pod Ultrasonic Cleaner for Oral Appliances
products.description:
The Zima Dental Pod is the one built specifically for oral appliances, from retainers and aligners to dentures and braces. Its frequency adjusts on its own between 42 and 47 kHz, and 42,000 Hz cavitation reaches grooves a brush cannot. It runs two cycles, a standard clean for daily use and a Max Clean for heavier buildup after travel or a gap in routine.

The design is described as non-abrasive and compact enough for a daily bathroom counter. The listing mentions a dental product award, a recognition claim we noted without ranking on. The tank size and noise level are not stated, so check fit with your denture, and there is no UV option mentioned.

A 12-month warranty comes with a promised support reply within one business day. Day to day it is a rinse-and-go pod that stays on the counter. Compared with the 7MAGIC at 48 kHz and four modes it keeps the process simpler, and unlike the fixed 45 kHz ACMEZING it adapts frequency during the cycle.
products.bestFor: Denture, retainer and guard wearers who want a pod designed only for oral appliances.
pros: Frequency adjusts on its own between 42 and 47 kHz during a cycle
Designed for retainers, aligners, guards, dentures and braces
Max Clean mode tackles heavier buildup after travel or a gap
A 12-month warranty with support replies in one business day
cons: Only two modes are offered, standard and Max Clean, with no other options
Tank size and noise level are not stated, so check the fit first

products.name: MUAYSY 45kHz Ultrasonic Denture Cleaner, 4 Modes

specList.label: Lid
specList.value: Two holes for brushes and heat

products.description:
The MUAYSY combines 45,000 Hz ultrasonic cleaning with four UV lamps in a compact 200 ml unit. You can run ultrasonic and UV together in a fast or deep mode, or run either one alone, giving four modes in all. The UV lamps turn off when the lid opens.

A double-hole lid lets you stand a toothbrush or makeup brush in the unit, and the holes also help dissipate heat. The listing's strongest percentage claims are marketing figures we did not rely on, and the UV is an extra and not a replacement for rinsing or brushing. At 200 ml it is limited for a full denture.

It is light enough for the office, a bathroom or travel, and the mode variety makes it more flexible than a two-button pod. Against the CXRUY it offers the same 45 kHz with more combinations, and compared with the 7MAGIC at 48 kHz it has a lower frequency and no stated noise or water-resistance rating. It is a decent choice for a user who likes choosing between ultrasonic and UV.
products.bestFor: Wearers who like to choose between ultrasonic, UV or combined cycles in a small pod.

The 45,000 Hz setting is gentle on thin plastic dental appliances

buyingCriteria.explanation: A pod only works if the appliance sits in the water without leaning on the walls, and many pods are sized for retainers. Almost every pod here lists 200 ml, which suits a retainer, an aligner tray or a partial more comfortably than a full set. The 7MAGIC, UEOFEN, CXRUY and MUAYSY all list 200 ml, and the ACMEZING says it can hold up to three retainers. Measure your denture against the interior before you buy, and read the listing for the tank depth.

Frequency controls how harsh the bubbles are, and a higher number is gentler. For plastics and denture materials, 42 kHz and above is the usual comfortable range. The Zima adjusts between 42 and 47 kHz, the ACMEZING, UEOFEN, CXRUY and MUAYSY run at 45 kHz, and the 7MAGIC runs at 48 kHz. Check your dentist's guidance on cleaning products and heat, since ultrasonic cleaning does not replace professional care.

Cycle choice affects how much wear each clean applies. Five minutes is a normal daily run, and 10 minutes is a heavier option, with pulse cycles being gentler in rhythm. The 7MAGIC and ACMEZING give four modes, the MUAYSY gives four ultrasonic and UV combinations, the UEOFEN and CXRUY give two, and the Zima gives standard and Max Clean. Choose four modes if you share the pod, and two if you want to set and forget.

buyingCriteria.criterion: UV lights and what they do
buyingCriteria.explanation: UV is an optional extra and not a cleaning guarantee. The 7MAGIC, ACMEZING, CXRUY, MUAYSY and UEOFEN all add UV lights, usually four, while the Zima does not list any. Look for lights that switch off when the lid opens, as the 7MAGIC and MUAYSY do. Treat UV as a convenience feature, and always rinse the appliance after a cycle.

A pod usually lives on a bathroom counter, so noise and splash tolerance matter. The 7MAGIC lists below 42 dB and IPX5 water resistance, while the ACMEZING lists about 45 dB and the UEOFEN below 45 dB. The CXRUY and MUAYSY give no figures. For a shared bathroom or a bedroom, aim for under 45 dB and look for an IPX rating.

Little extras make a daily routine easier, and a warranty protects a machine used every day. The 7MAGIC includes a basket, tweezers, a brush, a cloth, an adapter and six tablets, and the UEOFEN and CXRUY include a tweezer. The Zima carries a 12-month warranty with a one-business-day support reply. Weigh what comes in the box, because tweezers help when lifting a wet denture without touching the water.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tank size and appliance fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank capacity and what each maker says it holds. Nearly every pod lists 200 ml, the ACMEZING says it holds up to three retainers, and the Zima does not state a size. We weighed fit for a full denture carefully, since a snug tank can touch the walls.

howWeEvaluated.title: Frequency and cycle choices
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stated frequency and the number of cleaning modes. The 7MAGIC leads at 48 kHz, the Zima adapts between 42 and 47 kHz, and four pods run at 45 kHz. The 7MAGIC and ACMEZING lead on mode choice at four each, while the UEOFEN and CXRUY offer two.

howWeEvaluated.title: UV features and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted which pods use UV and whether the lights switch off when the lid opens or the unit overheats. The CXRUY shuts off at 100°C, and the 7MAGIC and MUAYSY turn off UV when the lid opens. We treated UV as a convenience and not a hygiene claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise, water resistance and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated noise levels and water ratings. The 7MAGIC lists below 42 dB with IPX5, the ACMEZING about 45 dB, and the UEOFEN below 45 dB. We weighted these highly for bathroom and bedside use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Accessories, warranty and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at what each box includes and what support is promised. The 7MAGIC has the fullest kit with six tablets, and the Zima has a 12-month warranty with a one-business-day reply. We did not rank on price, only on what each pod offers for its class.

cards.label: Fixed frequency
cards.text: A single frequency is predictable and simple. The 7MAGIC at 48 kHz and the ACMEZING, UEOFEN, CXRUY and MUAYSY at 45 kHz all use one setting. Choose one if you like a known output and more modes or accessories.

cards.label: Adaptive frequency
cards.text: An adaptive pod changes its output through the cycle to spread energy. The Zima adjusts between 42 and 47 kHz on its own. Choose it if you want a dental-specific pod with a simple two-cycle layout and a warranty.

howToChoose.note: Fixed suits modes and kit seekers, and adaptive suits anyone who prefers simplicity.

faq.q: Which ultrasonic cleaner is best for dentures?
faq.a: The 7MAGIC is the best all-rounder here, with 48 kHz output, four modes, below 42 dB operation and IPX5 water resistance. The Zima is the purpose-built option with an auto-adjusting 42 to 47 kHz frequency. Because most pods hold 200 ml, check that your denture fits.

faq.q: Will a full denture fit in a 200 ml pod?
faq.a: It may be tight. Most pods here list 200 ml, which suits retainers, aligners and partials better than a full set. The denture must sit in the water without pressing the walls. Measure the interior, read the listing, and test with plain water before you buy or fill.

faq.q: Is an ultrasonic cleaner a replacement for brushing?
faq.a: No, it is a supplement. Ultrasonic cavitation loosens residue from ridges a brush cannot reach, but you should still rinse the denture and follow your dentist's routine. Use mild cleaning tablets only if the maker allows, as the 7MAGIC kit and UEOFEN listing do.

faq.q: Do UV lights make dentures sterile?
faq.a: Treat UV as an extra and not a guarantee. The 7MAGIC, ACMEZING, CXRUY, UEOFEN and MUAYSY add UV lights, and the Zima lists none. The 7MAGIC and MUAYSY switch the UV off when you open the lid. Rinse the appliance well afterward.

Avoid it unless your denture maker approves. Heat can warp some materials, and most small pods have no heater. The CXRUY shuts off automatically at 100°C, which shows the units can warm up. Use cool or lukewarm water and short cycles.

faq.q: How long should a cycle run?
faq.a: Five minutes is a normal daily cycle and 10 minutes is a deeper option. The 7MAGIC offers Quick 5 and Deep 10, the ACMEZING adds 5 and 10 minute pulse cycles, and the Zima has Max Clean. Start short, and only extend if residue remains.

faq.q: How do I look after the pod?
faq.a: Empty and dry the tank after each use so mineral film does not build up, and never run it without liquid. The 7MAGIC's IPX5 rating tolerates splashes, and the ACMEZING's silicone pads reduce vibration. Wipe the outside with a damp cloth and keep it away from direct heat.
